extracted.intended_audience: members of the Presbytery, Presbyterian ministers, and informed church members/Readers interested in Presbyterian doctrinal standards
extracted.subtask_description: A concise declaration of the Presbytery's principles regarding doctrine, worship, discipline, and government (14 heads), setting orthodox positions and condemning contrary doctrines in light of Scripture and the Confession/Catechisms. Intended to define ecclesiastical fellowship and guide church practice and testimony-bearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: I. Of God
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgement that there is one infinite, eternal, self‑existent and independent Being who subsists in three distinct persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) of one undivided essence and godhead; all equally the same in substance, power and glory though distinguished by personal properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms Trinitarian doctrine with scriptural citations (Deut. vi.4; Matt. xxviii.19; 1 Cor. viii.6; 1 Tim. i.17; 1 John v.7) and references to the Confession of Faith and Catechisms. Serves as the foundational affirmation for all other doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: II. Of the Holy Scriptures
rubrics_metrics.description: The light of nature is insufficient for saving knowledge; God has given a most perfect revelation of himself in the Old and New Testaments, which are of divine authority and the sole perfect and complete rule of faith and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scriptural warrants cited (Rom. i; 2 Tim. iii; 2 Pet. i); the Scriptures are the supreme judge to which all doctrines and controversies must be brought. References to Confession chap.1 and Catechisms. Rejects any authority other than God as author of Scripture.

rubrics_metrics.name: III. Of the Decrees of God
rubrics_metrics.description: Jehovah, by an immanent eternal act of will, purposed and decreed all events; by his absolute sovereignty he unchangeably determined the final state of all intelligent beings, predestinating a definite number to eternal life while passing by others to just punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms classical doctrine of divine decrees/predestination with scriptural citations (Rom. ix; Eph. i; Jude) and links to Confession chap.3 and Catechisms. Emphasizes sovereignty and the eternal counsel of God as the basis of salvation and reprobation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IV. Of Creation
rubrics_metrics.description: God created all beings, framed them with natures suited to their ends, preserves and upholds them by providence, and created man as an intelligent being in God's image with a reasonable immortal soul; God entered into a covenant with Adam as public head promising life on condition of perfect obedience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Genesis and other scriptures (Gen. i; Col. i; Rom. xi) and Confession/Catechism references. Stresses continual providence, the original image of God in man, and the covenant‑headship of Adam as foundational for later doctrines (sin, covenant theology).

rubrics_metrics.name: V. Of the Fall of Man
rubrics_metrics.description: The first parents sinned, lost original rectitude and were cut off from grace; as public person Adam's posterity inherit guilt, depravity, and inability to convert themselves — totally depraved and incapable of contributing to salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains original sin, total depravity, and inability with scriptural citations (Gen. iii; Rom. v; Rom. iii; Eph. ii) and Confession/Catechism refs. Affirms that means of grace are to be used but cannot of themselves secure conversion. Rejects any natural or moral ability as adequate for salvation.

rubrics_metrics.name: VI. Of the Covenant of Grace
rubrics_metrics.description: God entered into an eternal covenant of redemption with Jesus Christ as the federal head/second Adam; Christ fulfilled righteousness and bore punishment on behalf of the elect so that salvation is free to sinners and not of debt but of grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames redemption as a covenant transaction between Father and Son; cites Psalms, Isaiah, Matthew, and Confession chap.7 with Catechism references. Emphasizes that the covenant is a free grant contingent on Christ's satisfaction and mediatorial work.

rubrics_metrics.name: VII. Of the Mediator
rubrics_metrics.description: Jesus Christ, the eternal Son, assumed human nature in a personal union with the divine, is fully qualified as prophet, priest and king, and is appointed mediator and surety of the new covenant; his two natures remain distinct without confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details Christ's person and offices, his incarnation, atoning sacrifice, priesthood, kingship, and continuing mediatorial work (Hebrews, John, 1 Tim. refs). Ties to Confession chap.8 and Catechism questions. Describes his ongoing governance and application of redemption by Spirit and Word.

rubrics_metrics.name: VIII. Of the Gospel Offer
rubrics_metrics.description: God, in love and on the footing of Christ's sufficient sacrifice, makes a full, free and unhampered offer of Christ and salvation to sinners everywhere; ministers are to publish this offer without distinction and assure sinners of God's mercy and ability to save.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms a universal proclamation of the gospel and a frank ministerial offer (Rom. x; Isa. lv; Mark xvi; John iii; Confess. chap.7; Catechisms). States there are no external impediments between Christ held forth in the gospel and sinners appropriating him.

rubrics_metrics.name: IX. Of Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The active and passive obedience of Christ is the only meritorious cause of a sinner's justification; true and saving faith (a gift of God) is the sole instrumental cause by which the soul is interested in Christ and his righteousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains forensic justification by Christ's righteousness received by faith; cites Rom., Gal., Eph., Acts, and Confession chap.11 with Catechism refs. Distinguishes justification from law‑works and clarifies believers' relation to the moral law (rule of life) though freed from covenant of works.

rubrics_metrics.name: X. Of Good Works
rubrics_metrics.description: Truly good works are only those performed by a person united to Christ by faith and under the Spirit; the unregenerate's actions, however outwardly lawful, are not pleasing to God nor prepare for receiving grace; even believers' best works do not merit pardon or God's favor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that obedience springs from faith and the Spirit, motives must be God‑centred (not self‑interest), and works are evidential not meritorious. Provides scriptural citations (Gen., Heb., Matt., Eph., Titus) and references to Confession chap.16 and Catechisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: XI. Of Assurance of Grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Although believers may experience doubts, darkness or shaken assurance, in the actual saving acts of true faith there is objective assurance and confident trust in Christ and the promise of life; subjective assurance may develop slowly and be interrupted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes psychological/spiritual difficulties while affirming objective assurance in saving faith; cites Isa., Mark, 1 John, Psalms and Confession chap.18 with Catechism questions. Distinguishes between trouble in assurance and the reality of saving faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: XII. Of the Perseverance of the Saints
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who truly believe and are redeemed will never be totally subverted in faith; by God's immutability, Christ's efficacy and the Spirit's abiding, believers shall certainly and infallibly persevere in grace unto final salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms eternal security/perseverance with scriptural supports (Heb. xi; John x; Phil. i; 1 Pet. ii) and Confession/Catechism references. Acknowledges trials and remaining corruption but insists on ultimate perseverance and final glorification.

rubrics_metrics.name: XIII. Of Liberty of Conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Conscience is God's deputy in the soul and is subject only to God's revealed will; human commands bind only insofar as they agree with Scripture; believers have liberty from ceremonial law but may not, under pretense of conscience, indulge forbidden lusts or reject divine ordinances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances liberty with subjection to Scripture, condemns toleration of heresy by civil law as destructive of true religion, and holds that deviation from scriptural institutions merits ecclesiastical discipline. Cites James, Romans, Acts, Matthew, Deuteronomy and Confession chap.20 and Catechisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: XIV. Of Testimony‑Bearing
rubrics_metrics.description: All true believers are united to Christ and mutually bound to exercise commanded duties to preserve grace in themselves and one another; the visible church is externally in covenant, holds same faith and sacraments (baptism, Lord's Supper), and must maintain holy communion, fellowship, and public testimony against errors and enemies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes ecclesial unity, mutual pastoral duties, adherence to covenantal standards, and public testimony (history/argument as testimony). Directs visible church members to hold fast to Christ, maintain standards of doctrine and worship, and lift 'the banner of divine truth' in opposition to error.
